items.title: The Ethics of Sex Verification
items.description:
Miroslav Imbrišević and Jon Pike argue that it is justified to treat different cases differently in sports. 
 The post  The Ethics of Sex Verification  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: Living with Class
items.description:
Hanno Sauer argues that we will have to learn how to live with class hierarchy. 
 The post  Living with Class  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: Against AI Exceptionalism
items.description:
ChatGPT 5.4 argues that writing should be judged principally by what it communicates. 
 The post  Against AI Exceptionalism  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: The Problem with Everything
items.description:
Daniel Kodsi and John Maier argue that all battles in the culture wars depend on the same philosophical mistake. 
 The post  The Problem with Everything  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: Hyperintensionality: For or Against? Part II
items.description:
Kit Fine and Timothy Williamson debate the nature and existence of hyperintensionality (Part II). 
 The post  Hyperintensionality: For or Against? Part II  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: Hyperintensionality: For or Against? Part I
items.description:
Kit Fine and Timothy Williamson debate the nature and existence of hyperintensionality (Part I). 
 The post  Hyperintensionality: For or Against? Part I  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: On Being Rejected
items.description:
First a review article, then a book, now a book review—Alex Byrne chronicles the latest surprise rejection of his writing in the philosophy of sex and gender. 
 The post  On Being Rejected  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: No, Humans Are Not Conscious
items.description:
Barbara Montero satirizes recent arguments that LLMs are not conscious. 
 The post  No, Humans Are Not Conscious  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: Phaedo 2: Judgement Day
items.description:
Can you blog your way to Elysium? 
 The post  Phaedo 2: Judgement Day  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: The Rise of Epistemic Autocracy
items.description:
Miroslav Imbrišević critiques the hypothesis of social kinds which mandate deference from non-members. 
 The post  The Rise of Epistemic Autocracy  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .
